claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional third-place source group as one row containing No.3 Trainer at source index 176.
Bulbapedia says No.3 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a third-place prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer iteration was first awarded to the third-place winners of each regional Japanese World Challenge Summer event held between July and August 2000, with the circuit split into Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle events.

Bulbapedia says overall winners of the Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented their country in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii, while the remaining top-ranking players competed in a domestic Best in Japan final, both held in late August 2000; this dossier does not treat regional third place as the Hawaii representative slot.

Bulbapedia describes Tropical Mega Battle as an international TCG tournament held annually from 1999 through 2001 at Hilton Hawaiian Village in Honolulu, involving top players from Canada, Latin America, Europe, the United States, and Japan, with about 50 players each year.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference and were Non Holofoil.

Bulbapedia says two base versions of the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer exist, one depicting a male Trainer and the other a female Trainer, with the awarded version depending on the winner's gender.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.3 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Bulbapedia distinguishes the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle No.3 Trainer print, which featured Exeggutor and event-logo artwork by Ken Sugimori and Hiromi Ito, from the later World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer iteration.

Bulbapedia says third-place winners of the Secret Super Battle and Tropical Mega Battle Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.3 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration, so those final-stage photo cards must be separated from this non-holo regional third-place class.

Pokumon identifies Boy TMB No.3 Trainer as a World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle 2000 regional third-place prize, a Japanese unnumbered non-holo Trainer Winner card illustrated by Ken Sugimori, and gives an estimated copy count; this dossier treats that count as a collector estimate, not official disclosure.

As judged collector texture, the regional No.3 Trainer matters because third place is still a named, printed position in the event architecture: a podium edge where the bracket leaves a physical trace.

narrative.human_title: No.3 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional]: the podium edge
narrative.why_it_matters: No.3 Trainer is where the trophy line becomes most human. First place is clean victory; second place is near-miss; third place is the proof that even the outer edge of the podium mattered enough to personalize, print, and preserve. In the World Challenge Summer Tropical Mega Battle route, that means a player's name, conference, gendered base art, and rank all survive as one unnumbered card. It is not just scarcity. It is organized play learning to remember more than only the winner.
not_claiming: that every No.3 Trainer listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.3 Trainer, World Challenge, Tropical Mega Battle, regional third place, TMB, third-place winner, male Trainer, female Trainer, personalized name, Best in Japan, Exeggutor, or photo trophy.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.3 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the exact route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.3 Trainer / Ｎｏ.３トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional third-place prize, not Secret Super Battle, Best in Japan, 1999 Tropical Mega Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, or World Championships.

Check whether the card is the 2000 World Challenge Summer regional version: non-holo, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male or female Trainer artwork depending on winner gender.

Do not treat regional third place as the same as the Hawaii representative slot. Bulbapedia's Hawaii language belongs to overall winners, while remaining top-ranking players fed into domestic Best in Japan.
Separate this regional non-holo card from Best in Japan final No.3 Trainer cards, which Bulbapedia describes as Holofoil cards with the player's photograph superimposed on the illustration.
Separate this card from the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle No.3 Trainer, especially if a listing emphasizes Exeggutor or logo artwork by Ken Sugimori and Hiromi Ito.
Record Pokumon copy counts only as collector estimates. Do not convert them into official print-run facts.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including name/conference personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that No.3 Trainer name alone identifies the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

narrative.human_title: No.3 Trainer: the bronze trace of a vanished bracket
narrative.why_it_matters: No.3 Trainer is a beautiful little argument against only remembering winners. It says the tournament had enough structure, ceremony, and affection to print the third-place player too. The card is personalized, regional, non-holo, and exacting; it is not a generic award. It is the bronze trace of a vanished bracket, and for an agent trying to understand trophy cards, that precision is the whole point.
